title: Execute Senshac legacy-to-modular cutover
description: Epic for completing the migration from archived NacoSolutions/senshac to the modular Senshac repositories. Every Warren run must be created against exactly one open Seeds item from this epic or a child task, and the run must report that tracker ID in its PR and final status. Work proceeds in bounded PRs with one owner repository, explicit acceptance criteria, cost cap, and green quality gates. Sequence: migrate web application; integrate content and Tina editorial model; validate media/R2 and platform infrastructure; run route/SEO/accessibility/performance/rollback acceptance; then promote and begin redesign. Archived senshac remains the rollback source until acceptance is complete.

title: Define senshac-content cutover acceptance checklist
description: Define the Tina/content topology, local visual editing proof, pinned content build, media/R2 ownership, and reversible migration gates before moving production content from the archived monorepo.

title: Define senshac-web cutover and deployment contracts
description: Document Astro/Tina ownership, Cloudflare Pages deployment, R2/media boundaries, preview and production smoke checks, and rollback acceptance before moving the web implementation from the archived monorepo.

title: Consolidate modular local checkout and coordination state
description: Fetch current GitHub refs, preserve existing local work, normalize clean integration worktrees, audit Seeds/PR ownership, repair ignored repos registry bootstrap and document retained work. Keep active Warren branches intact.

title: Evaluate deferred Buzz deployment and Warren bridge plan
description: Plan consolidated from legacy senshac commit 1357df9 into docs/buzz-deployment-bridge-operations-plan.md. Resume after modular migration: deployment, identity, event schema, bridge and operations acceptance.

title: Reconcile archived monitoring issues with modular web follow-ups
description: Archived NacoSolutions/senshac retains 15 open PageSpeed/Lighthouse issues (#31-35,39,44,46-53). Assess current modular deployment performance, create actionable web-local Seeds with evidence, then close superseded legacy GitHub issues when archive administration is available.
